speed-calculator.name: Speed Calculator
speed-calculator.tagline: Solve any speed, distance, or time problem — with unit conversions and running pace.
speed-calculator.metaTitle: Speed Calculator – Distance, Time & Pace Solver | JaurTools
speed-calculator.metaDescription: Free speed calculator. Solve for speed, distance or time, with km/h, m/s, mph conversions and min/km pace — 100% in your browser.
speed-calculator.keywords: speed calculator, distance time speed solver, pace calculator, kmh to mph, average speed calculator
speed-calculator.quickAnswer: Pick what to solve for, enter the other two values, and the tool computes the third instantly. Speed equals distance divided by time: 100 km in 1.5 hours is 66.67 km/h, which is also 18.52 m/s, 41.43 mph, or a 0:54 min/km running pace.
keyFacts: The speed–distance–time triangle: cover the value you want — speed = distance ÷ time, distance = speed × time, time = distance ÷ speed.
1 m/s equals 3.6 km/h; 1 km/h equals 0.621371 mph.
Running pace is the inverse of speed: minutes per kilometer instead of kilometers per hour.
Average speed over a trip can hide variation — traffic jams and rest stops lower the average below your cruising speed.
Unit consistency matters: 100 km in 90 minutes is 66.67 km/h only after converting 90 minutes to 1.5 hours.
A knot — used in aviation and shipping — equals 1.852 km/h; 100 km/h is about 54 knots.
howTo: Choose whether to solve for speed, distance, or time.
Enter the two values you know — distance in km, time in hours, or speed in km/h.
Read the solved value highlighted at the top of the results.
Check the conversions: m/s, mph, total minutes, miles, and running pace.
Switch modes to answer the reverse question without retyping everything.
Use the pace readout to plan race splits: a 60-minute 10K needs a 6:00 min/km pace.
speed-calculator.formula:
Speed    = Distance ÷ Time
Distance = Speed × Time
Time     = Distance ÷ Speed
m/s = km/h ÷ 3.6 | mph = km/h × 0.621371 | pace = 60 ÷ km/h (min/km)
speed-calculator.workedExample:
Distance 100 km, time 1.5 hours, solving for speed.
Speed = 100 ÷ 1.5 = 66.67 km/h
In m/s: 66.67 ÷ 3.6 = 18.52 m/s
In mph: 66.67 × 0.621371 = 41.43 mph
Pace: 60 ÷ 66.67 = 0.9 min/km = 0:54 per km
Distance in miles: 100 × 0.621371 = 62.14 miles
benefits: Answers all three question types in one tool — no separate converters needed.
Running pace included, so runners can plan splits directly.
Instant results as you drag the sliders — great for what-if planning.
Honest unit math with no rounding tricks hidden.
limitations: Computes average speed only — it cannot account for acceleration, stops, or traffic within the trip.
Assumes consistent units as labeled; mixing miles with km/h-style inputs will give wrong answers.
Not for navigation: real travel time depends on roads, traffic, and rest stops.
Extreme inputs (zero time) are guarded to zero rather than producing infinity.

faqs.q: What is the speed distance time triangle?
faqs.a: Write D over S×T in a triangle. Cover the unknown: D alone on top means S = D÷T; S×T side by side on the bottom means D = S×T; T = D÷S. This tool applies it for you.

faqs.q: How do I convert km/h to mph?
faqs.a: Multiply by 0.621371. So 100 km/h is 62.14 mph. To go back, divide mph by 0.621371 (or multiply by 1.60934).

faqs.q: What is running pace and how is it calculated?
faqs.a: Pace is minutes per kilometer — the inverse of speed. Divide 60 by your km/h speed: 12 km/h gives a 5:00 min/km pace.

faqs.q: Why is my average speed lower than my cruising speed?
faqs.a: Average speed divides total distance by total time, including stops and slow sections. Cruising speed ignores them, so the average is always lower on real trips.

faqs.q: Can I enter time in minutes?
faqs.a: Enter time in hours using decimals: 90 minutes is 1.5 hours, 45 minutes is 0.75 hours. The results also show total minutes for convenience.
